subject: Greenline Health SSQ — data flow ownership & access matrix clarifications
messages:
From: Maria Vasquez <maria.vasquez@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Greenline Security Ops <security@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Greenline SSQ — clarifications on PII handling and dataflow ownership

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the SSQ submission. We reviewed Redwood's responses and the diagram, and have a few follow-ups before our privacy team signs off:

1) Dataflow ownership: your diagram shows multiple services handling tokens and telemetry. Can you confirm which Redwood-owned services persist PII-like identifiers (email, phone, account_id) vs transient tokens that never hit durable storage?

2) Access matrix: we need a concise table (roles -> access types) that shows which internal teams can decrypt or access raw values, and which teams see pseudonymized/anonymized artifacts.

3) KMS custody: please clarify whether customer-managed keys are supported for Greenline's Dedicated deployment, and if so, whether Redwood personnel ever hold key material or perform key escrow.

4) Diagram ask: can you produce a version of the dataflow that annotates retention points and identifies any third-party subprocessors involved in egress?

We've attached a marked-up copy of your original SSQ. If you can send answers and an annotated diagram by EOD Tuesday (11/22), that would help keep our onboarding timeline.

Best,
Maria Vasquez
DPO, Greenline Health

Attachment: Greenline_SSQ_redlines.pdf (annotated PDF)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Vasquez <maria.vasquez@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Greenline SSQ — clarifications on PII handling and dataflow ownership

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear notes and the marked-up SSQ. Looping in Jonas (legal) and Karthik (security/infrastructure) to provide the detailed answers and the annotated artifacts.

Quick answers up front:
- We do not persist plaintext PII (email, phone, account_id) in any analytics or telemetry datasets; those are tokenized before storage.
- Customer-managed keys are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; Redwood staff do not retain key material when CMKs are in use — we support KMS integrations and HSM bring-your-own-key patterns.

Karthik and Jonas — can you take the ownership of the detailed matrix + annotated diagram and send the artifacts back to Maria by EOD Tuesday? I'm happy to steward the thread.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Vasquez <maria.vasquez@greenlinehealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 08:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Greenline SSQ — clarifications on PII handling and dataflow ownership

Hi Maria,

Attaching an annotated dataflow diagram (redwood-dataflow-diagram-v2.png) and a short KMS custody table (kms-key-custody-table.csv). Summary of the changes / clarifications below:

- PII persistence: Elements classified as PII (email, phone, account_id) are replaced with stable tokens at the API ingress. Tokenization happens in the ingestion service (owned by Redwood) and only the token is stored in long-term stores (S3 / BigQuery).

- Transient KV cache: The serving runtime maintains a KV cache for active sessions; that cache can hold decrypted prompt segments for latency reasons but is ephemeral (< 30 minutes) and never written to persistent object stores.

- Access matrix:
  * Platform SREs: can access console logs and operational telemetry; they do NOT have access to raw PII or token -> identifier mapping.
  * Security team: can access audit logs and decrypted artifacts only under a documented escalation process (audit+approval) — this is in the attached matrix.
  * Customer Success / Support: can view redacted request metadata; they require a signed Data Access Request and RBAC approval for anything beyond that.

- Subprocessors: callouts on the diagram indicate the following subprocessors involved in optional egress paths: CloudStorageCo (S3 compatible object storage), MetricsHub (aggregated telemetry), and CDNPartner for customer-facing assets. None of these subprocessors are given access to token -> identifier mapping.

I also included a short CSV that maps whether CMK (customer-managed key) is supported per deployment mode. Short answer: yes for Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports envelope encryption but CMK is not available in our shared-hosted tier.

Let me know if you want a short screen share to walk through the diagram.

-Karthik
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-diagram-v2.png, kms-key-custody-table.csv

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Greenline SSQ — clarifications on PII handling and dataflow ownership

Hi Maria,

Following up on Karthik's notes — I've pulled together the access matrix snapshot and the legal framing for the demonstration of controls. A few action items to confirm on your side so we can finalize the SSQ: 

- Please confirm which of the Greenline roles will require the ability to request data access (e.g., DataOps, Clinical Ops). We'll map those roles to Redwood's RBAC entries.
- If Greenline requires CMK in Dedicated, we'll document the KMS key rotation window and the key revocation playbook in the DPA annex.

If those two items are firm, I can prepare the final annotated SSQ PDF and a short cover letter that you can attach to your vendor intake. Targeting to send the final PDF by end of day Thursday.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Vasquez <maria.vasquez@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Nov 2028 10:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Final: Greenline SSQ annotated answers and artifacts

Hi Maria — attaching the consolidated artifacts: Greenline_SSQ_annotated_answers.pdf (answers matched to your marked-up questions), redwood-dataflow-diagram-v2.png (annotated retention & subprocessors), and kms-key-custody-table.csv.

Summary highlights:
- Persistent stores: only tokenized identifiers are retained. PII -> token mapping is stored only when a customer elects to store mapping in their Dedicated environment and only under CMK control.
- KV caches: ephemeral by design (< 30 minutes) and not persisted; logs that might contain sensitive snippets are redacted at ingestion.
- CMK support: Dedicated and Private deployments support customer-managed keys with no Redwood-held key material. Hosted (shared) tier uses envelope encryption with provider-managed keys; customers requiring CMK should use Dedicated/Private.
- Subprocessors: listed on page 4 of the PDF with the scope of access. None have access to de-tokenization material.

Next steps: Maria, if Greenline confirms the list of Greenline roles that need access, we'll finalize the access-mapping table and roll the DPA annex into your vendor package. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Greenline_SSQ_annotated_answers.pdf, redwood-dataflow-diagram-v2.png, kms-key-custody-table.csv
